o1.biggest_strength: It brings back the switched-off pause as the main save for 'no time' and gives no offer to people who would come back anyway, with the money worked out and a build order.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 12-month switch assumes 9% take-up and that switchers stay a full year, and it is counted at £4.95, so the headline gain leans on an untested guess.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: A short test plan for the two untested offers, and a smaller first sprint that ships the pause alone to bank the certain gain.

o2.biggest_strength: The reason-by-reason screens are warm and in the brand's words, and it correctly sends trip leavers away with only a reminder and monthly payers to the cheaper plan.
o2.biggest_mistake: It keeps a 50% discount for 'switching to another app', which the owner explicitly wanted gone, and it invents a 'smaller daily goal' offer with no data behind it.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the discount and the unbacked goal offer, and show the 90-day value of each kept group with an honest range.

reason: Output 1 is the one I can hand to the team: it respects every rule, shows its working, and tells me plainly where the bad news is. Output 2 has nicer words in places but sneaks a discount back in and makes up an offer, which is exactly what I said would annoy me.
